name: Wild mushrooms (foraged fungi — porcini/boletus, chanterelle, morel, wild Agaricus, other wild species)

MeHg.control: Wild fungi DO have a mercury-methylation pathway and are documented mercury hyperaccumulators, so methylmercury is not dismissed as not-material for this subcategory. However, no government sets a methylmercury ML for any fungi in any jurisdiction; the methylmercury fraction is controlled by and bounded by the total-mercury ceiling for wild mushrooms (Israel FCS-2016 mushrooms tHg 30 ug/kg). No methylmercury ML exists to look up, and occurrence cannot supply the number.
MeHg.reference_method: MeHg by GC-ICP-MS / EN 16801 on any wild-mushroom lot whose total mercury approaches the tHg ceiling; wild-fungi methylmercury can be a material fraction of a high total-mercury result and must be characterised on elevated lots.

Cr-VI.control: No government sets a total-chromium or hexavalent-chromium maximum level for edible fungi in any jurisdiction. Chromium in the fungal matrix is dominated by nutritionally-essential Cr(III), and Cr(VI) reduces to Cr(III) in the organic-rich matrix. Firm control: reflex speciation - any total-Cr result >= 100 ug/kg triggers Cr(VI) speciation, and any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails; Cr(VI) is never a panel number.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Total-Cr screen by ICP-MS; on any result >= 100 ug/kg, Cr(VI) by EN 15192 / EPA 6800 IC-ICP-MS isotope-dilution; LOQ-level quantifiable Cr(VI) = fail.
Cr-VI.regulatory_basis: No regulatory total-Cr or Cr(VI) ML for edible fungi in any jurisdiction; the only register total-Cr MLs are for dairy powder, drinking water, and fertiliser.
Cr-VI.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915; EU 2024/1987; Switzerland VHK 2026; MERCOSUR GMC 12/2011; Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019; Israel FCS-2016; Codex; FDA; China GB 2762

Ni.control: No credible sovereign government sets a nickel maximum level for edible fungi in any jurisdiction; the EU 2024/1987 nickel regulation enumerates vegetables, legumes, nuts, and cereals but deliberately does not list fungi. Under the government-limit-only method HMTc publishes no standalone numeric nickel limit for this matrix; nickel is monitored on the mandatory total-element panel.
Ni.reference_method: Total-element screen by ICP-MS on every lot; investigate any elevated nickel result against grower substrate and provenance.

Sn.control: Every government tin maximum level in the register is scoped to canned / tin-coated product; tin migrates from tinplate, and that packaging-migration pathway is the contamination these MLs regulate (India even sets a canned-mushroom Sn ML of 250000 ug/kg). Fresh cultivated and wild mushrooms are not sold in tinplate, so that pathway is absent; any tin present is dietary background rather than tinplate migration. Canned mushrooms route to the canned-foods category and carry the tin ML there.
Sn.reference_method: Mandatory total-element screen by ICP-MS; tin is screened but not a binding numeric ceiling for fresh, non-canned product.
Sn.regulatory_basis: Tin MLs (incl. India canned mushrooms 250000 ug/kg) apply to canned product only; no fresh-fungi Sn ML exists in any jurisdiction.
Sn.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915; EU 2024/1987; Switzerland VHK 2026; MERCOSUR GMC 12/2011; Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019; Israel FCS-2016; Codex; FDA; China GB 2762

Al.control: No credible sovereign government sets an aluminium contaminant maximum for edible fungi. Under the government-limit-only method HMTc publishes no standalone numeric Al limit for this matrix; naturally present aluminium remains a surveillance issue governed by the additive rules of the markets of sale.
Al.reference_method: Screen total Al by ICP-MS and document any aluminium-containing processing aid; investigate elevated results and comply with all additive rules in markets of sale.

Cr.control: No credible sovereign government sets a total-chromium contaminant maximum for edible fungi in any jurisdiction (the only register total-Cr MLs are for dairy powder, drinking water, and fertiliser). Under the government-limit-only method HMTc publishes no standalone numeric total-Cr limit for this matrix; total chromium is monitored and hexavalent chromium is controlled by reflex speciation (see Cr-VI).
Cr.reference_method: Total-Cr screen by ICP-MS on every lot; investigate any elevated total-Cr result and reflex-speciate per the Cr-VI control.

method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; regulatory-alignment / read-across / not-material / control)
lineage: Cat-29 government-limit-default compile (HMTc Method v2.0). Anchors: EU Reg. 2023/915 (wild fungi Pb 800 / Cd 500; cultivated fungi Pb 300 / Cd 50; oyster+shiitake Cd 150), Switzerland VHK 2026 (wilde Pilze Pb 800 / Cd 500; Agaricus bisporus Cd 50), MERCOSUR GMC 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 (Agaricus/Pleurotus/Lentinula tAs 300), Israel FCS-2016 (fruits and vegetables including mushrooms: tHg 30 / iAs 60 / tAs 1000). Cultivated-cadmium split (common Cd 50 vs oyster/shiitake Cd 150 → cultivated-mushrooms-oyster-shiitake) ratified 2026-08-13 per OI-20260813-cultivated-mushroom-cd-split.
